text:
jordan: Heads-up — I noticed billing window drift after the last compaction run. Tenant A's final token totals were ~2% higher than expected once late events were applied. Looks like compaction + late arrivals are creating double-counts in a few edge cases. Anyone else seen this?

mira: I saw anomalies too, yes. It coincided with the shard compactor tweak we merged last week (https://git.internal/r/redwood/compactor/pulls/322). Could be tombstone vs overwrite ordering.

sam: Can you repro with a small trace? double-counts usually happen when dedupe keys diverge between first-seen and late-arrival fingerprints.

jordan: Repro (super-simplified): we get E1 {seq:100, fp=a, epoch:1, tokens:120} then a late E1' {seq:100, fp=a2, epoch:2, tokens:120}. Compactor currently keeps both because fingerprint differs, billing pipeline sums both -> double charge. My rough proposal: add an explicit `epoch` marker to the event envelope and have compactor maintain an "accepted-fingerprint" per sequence key; compactor should prefer event with highest epoch and emit reconciliation deltas if it replaces a previously-accepted fingerprint. Example envelope: `{"seq":100,"fp":"a","epoch":3}`.

mira: That reduces ambiguity but increases compactor state (per-seq accepted-fp). Also backfills/backfills need migration path (how do historical events get an epoch?).

sam: Another approach: compactor emits soft-deltas instead of full canonical events. On first-seen you emit +120 tokens for seq=100; when a late arrival reconciles you emit -120 then +120 (or just adjust to difference). Pros: compactor keeps less long-lived state, billing becomes additive. Cons: billing/ledger must accept negative deltas and we need strong idempotency.

jordan: Negative-deltas are workable — finance already supports post-facto credits — but ops will see a spike in credit events and alerts. Ledger idempotency is the big must-have.

devops-bot: deploy notice: compactor-v2 will roll to canary at 2026-03-18T02:00Z (build 2026.03.18-37). Watch `billing.deltas` and `compactor.reconciliations` dashboards.

mira: Another mitigation: enforce a configurable per-tenant watermark/grace window (default 2h). Only accept late events inside the grace; beyond that, route to backfill job with manual audit. That reduces surface area but could drop legitimately late telemetry.

sam: Proposed path: 1) implement soft-delta emit in compactor canary + metrics, 2) add optional `epoch` marker and reconciliation logic (opt-in per-tenant), 3) default grace window 2h (configurable) and backfill path for older late arrivals. I'll draft an RFC with perf/cost estimates.

jordan: +1. If we choose soft-delta we must update audit replay and invoice generator so replays produce the same net adjustments. Test plan idea: simulate bursts with delays 0–6h and assert net token delta equals ground truth after compaction + reconciliation. Also add mutation/property tests for idempotency.

mira: I'll own the test harness and create synthetic scenarios. sam — can you start the RFC and include benchmark matrix (state overhead vs ingest throughput vs invoice churn)?

sam: On it. I'll ping infra for quota to run a 10k tps simulation. Setting RFC tag `metering/compaction-reconcile`.

jordan: Thanks — adding follow-up: include an audit event type `reconcile.adjustment` with original_seq, old_fp, new_fp, delta_tokens so downstream accounting/audit can trace adjustments.

mira: Good call. That will help SRE and finance to correlate spikes.

sam: Ok spinning up a draft now, will drop link here when ready.

jordan: excellent. devops-bot — please post canary metrics after rollout? (reaction :eyes:)

devops-bot: scheduled metric snapshot will be posted to #eng-platform-canary at 2026-03-18T02:15Z.
